QpTopicAgreement.description:
A labeler's measured agreement with the ``qp-topic-v0`` reference raters.

Every quantity here is **agreement with the reference raters**, never
accuracy: reference error and labeler error cannot be separated, least of
all on the boundary labels, and a labeler of the reference raters' own
model family partly measures shared convention. The reference set's
two-block, outcome-stratified frame is disclosed in ``docs/qp-topic.md``;
the pooled rate here spans both streams, and the per-stream split is
derived at measurement review by joining the reference to the corpus's
dispositions — deliberately not carried in the committed artifacts. Only
reference entries the labeler actually covered are compared; the rest are
counted in ``uncovered``.

floor.description: What a constant labeler would score on the same compared entries — the largest reference class's share. An agreement rate is unreadable without it; the distance from it is the only part that is skill
floor.title: Floor

gate_passed.description: Overall agreement reached the publication gate **and** the run covered enough of the reference set to have measured the stream; failing either, a labeler publishes nothing
gate_passed.title: Gate Passed

overall_agree.description: Compared entries where the two labels match
overall_agree.title: Overall Agree

overall_n.description: Reference entries the labeler covered and compared
overall_n.title: Overall N

overall_rate.description: overall_agree / overall_n — agreement with the v0 reference rater, not accuracy. Null when nothing was compared
overall_rate.title: Overall Rate

per_label.description: Per-reference-label agreement, floor-gated, in the vocabulary's own alphabetical order
per_label.title: Per Label

triangle.description: The 3x3 confusion matrix on the constitutional-rights / criminal-law / civil-procedure triangle, one row per reference label
triangle.title: Triangle

uncovered.description: Reference entries the labeler produced no label for, so unmeasured
uncovered.title: Uncovered

QpTopicAgreement.title: QpTopicAgreement

QpTopicApplicationPublishedEntry.description:
One row of the accumulating application labels artifact.

A published label plus the extract shape it was read from, stamped by the
builder from the extract row and never by the labeler: a label read from a
caption and a stay request is weaker than one read from the application's
own text, and every cut reports the two apart (``docs/qp-topic.md``,
*Applications*).

batch.description: The labeling batch that first published this row (1-indexed)
batch.title: Batch

case_id.description: Canonical ``<court>/<docket>`` id — joins the corpus row and ``data/cases``
case_id.title: Case Id

docket_number.description: The Court's own docket number (e.g. ``25-52``) — the second half of the key pair the extract and reference joins are checked against
docket_number.title: Docket Number

input_kind.description: Which extract shape the label was read from: with the stored application text, or from the caption, court below and docket entries alone
input_kind.title: Input Kind

label.description: The primary ``qp-topic-v0`` label: mandatory, single, and the only field any published count sums over
label.title: Label

secondary.description: An advisory second subject for a smuggled question — never counted, and unpublishable in v0
secondary.title: Secondary

source.description: Where this row's published label came from: the labeler's own call, or the hand reference set's adjudicated label for a reference member
source.title: Source

vehicle.description: The petition asks for a GVR in light of a named decision; the label is the underlying subject. Recorded, unpublishable in v0
vehicle.title: Vehicle

QpTopicApplicationPublishedEntry.title: QpTopicApplicationPublishedEntry

QpTopicBatchEntry.description:
One labeling run's contribution to the accumulating labels artifact.

The artifact is the union of every batch, so without this ledger a reader
could not tell which run produced which row, what it was measured at, or how
many runs the file took. Each row records both counts because they answer
different questions: ``published`` is what the batch added to the file, while
``measured`` is what its labeler actually read — larger by the reference rows
it re-graded, which are the per-run cost of the measurement and publish
nothing new.

The measurement fields are kept per batch rather than only at the top level
so a drifting labeler is visible as a series rather than as a single current
number — with two readings the series will not support. Every batch is
scored over the **same** reference entries, so the differences between rows
are labeler-side re-labeling of identical items, not independent samples of
anything: a few points of movement on ``n`` this size is noise, and only a
sustained move reads. And ``agree``/``n`` never read without ``floor``, which
is why it is carried here rather than recomputed: on a sixteen-label
vocabulary most of any rate is the floor.

agree.description: Compared reference entries this batch matched
agree.title: Agree

disagreements.description: Of those, texts where this batch's labeler differed from the rule. The shadow rules are the only instrument that touches rows the batch publishes, so the series is the regression trip-wire; its level is uninterpretable
disagreements.title: Disagreements

fired.description: Texts in this batch exactly one shadow rule fired on
fired.title: Fired

floor.description: What a constant labeler scores on this batch's compared entries — the rate is unreadable without it, and only the distance above it is skill
floor.title: Floor

frame_rows.description: QP-bearing rows in the labeling frame when this batch was cut, as the extract counted them. The denominator that turns the labeled share of the frame from a bound into a measurement, at this batch's corpus vintage and no other's. None where the extract reported no count
frame_rows.title: Frame Rows

labeler.description: Who assigned this batch's labels — engine and model
labeler.title: Labeler

labeler_rows.description: Of those, rows carrying this labeler's own call. The remainder are reference members entering the artifact from the hand set's adjudicated labels, which no labeler assigned — so this, not `published`, is what a batch labeled
labeler_rows.title: Labeler Rows

measured.description: Extract rows this batch's labeler read — its new rows plus every reference row in the frame, re-graded for the measurement
measured.title: Measured

n.description: Reference entries this batch covered and compared
n.title: N

published.description: Rows this batch first published into the artifact
published.title: Published

superseded.description: Rows already in the artifact whose published label this batch changed. Only ever rows whose published label became the hand set's: a reference entry relabeled by hand, or a row the reference set has since taken in
superseded.title: Superseded

QpTopicBatchEntry.title: QpTopicBatchEntry

QpTopicLabelAgreement.description:
One label's agreement between a labeler and the v0 reference rater.

Counted over the reference entries carrying this label, so ``n`` is the
*reference* support, not the labeler's. ``rate`` is withheld below the
per-label support floor: under it the count is reported and the ratio is
not, because a single entry moves it by tens of points.

agree.description: Compared entries where the labeler assigned this label
agree.title: Agree

label.description: The reference label this row counts
label.title: Label

n.description: Compared reference entries carrying this label
n.title: N

rate.description: agree / n — agreement with the v0 reference rater, not accuracy. Null below the support floor, where the label is unmeasured in v0
rate.title: Rate

QpTopicLabelAgreement.title: QpTopicLabelAgreement

QpTopicShadow.description:
The deterministic shadow rules' standing disagreement with the agent labeler.

The rules publish nothing and pre-empt nothing: they are a regression
trip-wire, so a drifting labeler shows up as a moving disagreement rate
before it shows up in a published cut. **Only the movement is readable, not
the level**: the rules' precision was measured on the reference set and is
unmeasured on the labeled stream, which is denial-heavy where the reference
set is grant-enriched — so a disagreement here is as likely a rule being
wrong as a labeler being wrong. Compare a run only against another run of the
same labeler over the same extract.

``texts`` is the denominator that makes ``fired`` readable: without it a run
whose extract covered nothing reports the same clean zeros as a run no rule
happened to fire on.

disagreements.description: Of those, texts where the agent label differs from the rule's label
disagreements.title: Disagreements

fired.description: Of those, texts exactly one shadow rule fired on
fired.title: Fired

texts.description: Labeled cases the extract supplied a text for — the rules' denominator
texts.title: Texts

QpTopicShadow.title: QpTopicShadow

QpTopicTriangleRow.description:
One row of the ``constitutional-rights`` / ``criminal-law`` / ``civil-procedure`` matrix.

The row is a reference label; ``counts`` are the labeler's assignments over
the same three labels in that fixed order, so ``counts[i]`` of the row for
label *i* is the diagonal. A labeler label from outside the triangle lands
in ``other``, which keeps every row summing to ``n`` without widening the
matrix past the three labels whose boundaries are the error sink.

counts.description: Labeler assignments in the fixed order constitutional-rights, criminal-law, civil-procedure
counts.title: Counts

n.description: Compared reference entries carrying this row's label
n.title: N

other.description: Compared entries the labeler placed outside the three triangle labels
other.title: Other

reference.description: The reference label this row counts
reference.title: Reference

QpTopicTriangleRow.title: QpTopicTriangleRow

description:
``data/qp-topics/qp-topics-applications.json`` — the ``qp-topic-v1`` application labels.

The application frame's counterpart to :class:`QpTopicLabels`, kept in a file
of its own so the petition artifact and every reader of it are untouched and
the application gate binds apart from the petition gate. It accrues the same
way, batch by batch, and a reference member publishes the application
reference block's adjudicated label rather than the labeler's. ``agreement``
and ``shadow`` describe the most recent run only, measured against the
application reference block; ``batches`` keeps every run's figures, and each
ledger row's ``frame_rows`` counts the application frame.

Written only when the application gate passes. Agreement here is with the
block's adjudicated labels, not accuracy, and the block's raters and fitted
rules are disclosed in ``docs/qp-topic.md``. Labels here are a corpus
description, not a prediction claim, and nothing frozen reads them.

agreement.description: The most recent run's measured agreement with the application reference block

batches.description: One row per labeling run that contributed, in batch order
batches.title: Batches

cases.description: Labeled applications across every batch (== len(entries))
cases.title: Cases

entries.description: One entry per labeled application, in case_id order, across every batch
entries.title: Entries

extract_rule.description: The extract rule whose rows every label was read from
extract_rule.title: Extract Rule

labeler.description: Who assigned the most recent batch's labels — engine and model. Earlier batches carry their own labeler in `batches`
labeler.title: Labeler

shadow.description: The most recent run's shadow-rule counts over the stored application text

vocabulary.description: The label vocabulary every entry draws from
vocabulary.title: Vocabulary

title: QpTopicApplicationLabels
